\section[el alojamiento]{el alojamiento — the accommodation, the lodging}

\label{lesson:ES-C660-alojamiento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the sailor, then the Spanish for the captain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el alojamiento}
\textbf{el alojamiento} — \textquotedblleft{}the accommodation, the lodging\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El precio incluye el alojamiento.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The price includes accommodation.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Alojamiento y desayuno} — bed and breakfast.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{alojamiento} is built on \emph{alojar} \textquotedblleft{}to lodge\textquotedblright{}, which came from Occitan \emph{alotjar} (EtymDB), built on a Germanic word for a shelter or hut.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el alojamiento}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el alojamiento}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el alojamiento}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the sailor, then the Spanish for the captain, then say \emph{el alojamiento} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el alojamiento mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The accommodation, the lodging\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[alojarse]{alojarse — to stay (at a hotel or a house), to lodge}

\label{lesson:ES-C660-alojarse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the captain, then the Spanish for the accommodation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: alojarse}
\textbf{alojarse} — \textquotedblleft{}to stay (at a hotel or a house), to lodge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Nos alojamos en un hotel del centro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We are staying at a hotel in the centre.}
\end{quote}

Without \emph{se}, \emph{alojar} is to put someone up.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{alojarse} comes from Occitan \emph{alotjar} \textquotedblleft{}to lodge\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), which is built on a Germanic word for a shelter or hut.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{alojarse}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{alojarse}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{alojarse}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the captain, then the Spanish for the accommodation, then say \emph{alojarse} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does alojarse mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To stay (at a hotel or a house), to lodge\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[hospedarse]{hospedarse — to stay as a guest}

\label{lesson:ES-C660-hospedarse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the accommodation, then the Spanish for to stay.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: hospedarse}
\textbf{hospedarse} — \textquotedblleft{}to stay as a guest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se hospedó en casa de unos amigos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He stayed at some friends’ house.}
\end{quote}

A close twin of \emph{alojarse}, very common in Latin America.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{hospedarse} is inherited from Late Latin \emph{hospitāre} (EtymDB), Latin \emph{hospitārī} \textquotedblleft{}to be a guest, to put up\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{hospes} \textquotedblleft{}guest, host\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hospedarse}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hospedarse}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{hospedarse}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the accommodation, then the Spanish for to stay, then say \emph{hospedarse} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[el hostal]{el hostal — the guesthouse, the small hotel}

\label{lesson:ES-C660-hostal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to stay, then the Spanish for to stay as a guest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el hostal}
\textbf{el hostal} — \textquotedblleft{}the guesthouse, the small hotel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El hostal es barato y limpio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The guesthouse is cheap and clean.}
\end{quote}

In Spain \emph{un hostal} is a modest, often family-run hotel.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{hostal} is inherited through Old Spanish \emph{ostal} (EtymDB) from Late Latin \emph{hospitāle} \textquotedblleft{}a guest house\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{hospes} \textquotedblleft{}guest\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to stay, then the Spanish for to stay as a guest, then say \emph{el hostal} again

\section[el albergue]{el albergue — the hostel; the shelter}

\label{lesson:ES-C660-albergue}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to stay as a guest, then the Spanish for the guesthouse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el albergue}
\textbf{el albergue} — \textquotedblleft{}the hostel; the shelter\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dormimos en un albergue juvenil.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We slept in a youth hostel.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Albergue juvenil} — youth hostel.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{albergue} is built on \emph{albergar} \textquotedblleft{}to shelter\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), which comes from a Germanic compound \emph{heriberga} \textquotedblleft{}a shelter for an army\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{harjaz} \textquotedblleft{}army\textquotedblright{} and \emph{bergô} \textquotedblleft{}shelter\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
